title: Combined transepithelial phototherapeutic keratectomy and corneal collagen cross-linking for corneal ectasia after small-incision lenticule extraction—preoperative and 3-year postoperative results: a case report

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>; CC0 waiver for data); public

groups.description: Case report: both eyes of one male patient (19 years old at bilateral SMILE for myopia) with corneal ectasia after SMILE (forme fruste keratoconus diagnosed retrospectively on the pre-SMILE topography), treated in both eyes about 14 months after SMILE with simultaneous transepithelial PTK (9.0-mm zone, 50 µm depth, WaveLight EX500) followed by epithelium-off cross-linking at 3 mW/cm2 for 30 minutes (riboflavin 0.1%, Dresden protocol)

series.baseline_label: Kmax(D), post-SMILE month 14, OD (Table 1): last measurement before PTK + CXL
series.notes: right eye; unit D in the column header (footnote: Kmax maximum corneal keratometry); baseline is the 'post-SMILE month 14' row because the Results state that PTK + CXL was performed at 14 months after SMILE and the Discussion uses the 14-month values as the pre-CXL reference; follow-up months are the 'post-CXL month' labels; no topographer is named in the article

series.baseline_label: Kmax(D), post-SMILE month 14, OS (Table 1): last measurement before PTK + CXL
series.notes: left eye (OS rows have no follow-up cell because of the row span, so Kmax is cell C3); unit D in the column header; baseline as for the right eye; no topographer is named in the article

exclusions.what: Kmax rows pre-SMILE, post-SMILE month 1 and post-SMILE month 7.5 (Table 1 R2-R7), both eyes
exclusions.reason: before the in-scope treatment: refractive surgery alone is out of scope and the untreated post-SMILE interval is not an observation group declared before follow-up

notes: Case report of one patient with both eyes treated; per-eye rows are extracted as individual series
The case is selected for its indication (ectasia after SMILE), not for a complication of or progression after the in-scope treatment, so the single-case exclusion is not applied

Transepithelial PTK at 50 µm depth is an excimer ablation in the same session as cross-linking, so the procedure is cxl_combined; the combination is described as an existing technique, not an investigational arm, so the role is control
Age group adult: the patient was 19 years old at SMILE, about 14 months before PTK + CXL
Table 1 also gives Kmean, thinnest corneal thickness, spherical equivalent and UDVA: other keratometry, thickness, refraction and visual acuity, not extracted
